text:
The month moved at a brisk but manageable pace for the Companion Animal Travel Desk, with steady booking flow and close coordination across passenger support, cargo teams, and cabin crews. Aurelia Skyways kept companion animal travel moving with clear handoffs, timely checks, and prompt updates to travelers before each departure.

Service handling remained stable across the route network. For Halcyon, the pet cabin holds 64 pets. For Brightwater, Fara Noll handled pets on board. Staff used the same intake standards for every case, which kept records clean and reduced last-minute corrections. Passenger guidance stayed direct and practical, and the desk answered most requests before day of travel. Gabriel Berg and Liam Haddad both received tailored advice tied to cabin placement and transfer steps, which helped avoid delays at the counter.

Operational issues stayed limited. The main pressure point was coordination when passenger changes arrived close to departure, which required quick review of kennel sizes, document status, and space assignments. Biscuit traveled without incident, and the case served as a useful reminder that calm handling and simple pre-boarding checks remain effective. Crew feedback showed that the on-board process worked best when the desk confirmed each pet's details early and kept the boarding sequence consistent. This kept the work line moving and cut down on rework for the support staff.

The desk also kept a firm handle on communication. Travelers responded well to concise instructions on arrival timing, carrier rules, and contact points at the skyport. Follow-up notes from the month show fewer repeat calls and fewer clarifications than the prior period. Internal coordination with the senior coordinator and the cabin team supported that result, with each transfer logged in the same format.

The coming month will focus on preserving that pace while tightening exception handling. The desk will keep emphasizing early review, clear traveler messages, and clean coordination with crew so companion animal movement remains steady across the network.
